note: ADR-0037 / PRD decision 40.5 — the agent domain's cut at the assembled edge. `bind.py` now derives a tool's argument schema from a route's OpenAPI `requestBody` as well as its `parameters`, so a JSON-body route binds when — and only when — FastAPI publishes it against a real pydantic model: `POST /api/workspace/new` (`WorkspaceNewBody`, one named field `name`) is `workspace_new` below. Three JSON-body routes remain UNBINDABLE, for a different reason than before: `PUT /api/workspace/file` (`workspace_write`), `POST /api/workspace/entity` (`entity_upsert`) and `POST /api/claims` (`propose`) each take a bare `body: dict = Body(...)`, which FastAPI publishes as `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}` with NO named `properties` — there is nothing in that shape for `bind.py` to derive a per-argument schema from, or check a manifest's declared arguments against. Closing this gap needs those three routes moved to named pydantic body models in `core/agent/control_plane/routers/workspaces.py` + `api_shared.py` first — an agent-api change, not an assembler one, and out of scope here. Tracked, with the full tool-by-tool breakdown, at the issue this manifest shipped with.

tools.name: workspace_tree
tools.note: The file listing for the caller's own workspace, or one of their shared workspaces named by `slug`. `hidden` includes dotfiles.

tools.name: workspace_read
tools.note: Read one file's content by its relative path. `slug` selects a shared workspace; omitted, it is the caller's own.

tools.name: workspace_purpose
tools.note: Reads the one-line PURPOSE a workspace carries. The SET side (`POST /api/workspace/purpose`) IS bindable now (`WorkspacePurposeBody` is a named pydantic model) but is not wired in as a tool here: it would need a name of its own — this GET's name is already `workspace_purpose` in the worker's allow-list (`core/agent/worker/mcp_tools.v1.json`) — and minting a new one is a worker-capability decision, not an assembler one. Left as the concrete next step in the issue this manifest shipped with.

tools.name: workspace_new
tools.note: CREATE a brand-new blank workspace, seeded from the template, and add it to the caller's active set. `name` is optional (`WorkspaceNewBody.name`) — omitted, the route mints a unique default label.
